column1: # Dormancy registry for the in-process alert rules (`observability.infra_watch.rules`
# in files/cogneva.json).
# These rules run inside the application, not in Prometheus, and they have no
# query API: this chart file is the only source of truth for their expressions.
# The witness reading (scripts/host/cogneva-alert-rule-witness-reading.sh in the
# private brain repo, COGNEVA_RULE_LAYER=infra_watch) checks each rule's vector
# selectors against the live series face and the 24h sample window, exactly as
# it does for the Prometheus layer.
# A rule whose series do not exist cannot fire, and that looks the same as a
# rule that found nothing wrong. Sleeping is not automatically a defect, but the
# reason has to be written down where a reader (and the reading) can find it:
#     rule <tab> absent_series (comma separated) <tab> reason <tab> why
# reason is a closed set:
#   object_absent     the object family is not deployed; the rule wakes with it
#   component_absent  the component the rule watches is not deployed -- a defect
#   feature_off       the feature is not configured
#   collector_off     the exporter is up but this collector is not enabled
#   exporter_version  the source binary's version does not expose the family
#   series_renamed    upstream renamed/removed the series; the rule needs a fix
#   known_defect      a declared defect, with the fix named in why
#   lazy_counter      the series is created by the first bad event; no event so
#                     far means nothing to fire on, and the rule fires the
#                     moment one happens (absence is the good outcome)
#   error_only_state  the gauge is exported only for problem states; a healthy
#                     subject is absent rather than zero (absence is the good
#                     outcome)
#   code_not_deployed the emitting code is newer than the running image; the
#                     series appears on the next rollout, at which point this
#                     row is reported stale and must be deleted
# An absent series without a row here exits 1. An unknown reason code, an empty
# why, or a missing registry exits 3. A row whose series came back is reported
# as stale -- the condition it describes is no longer true.
# The last two codes are the ones to watch: they turn "nothing happened" into a
# legitimate dormant rule, so a wholesale application of them would silently
# wave through a dead rule. Each row names the emitting path in why.
# Re-read 2026-10-19 against the live series face (24h window), app image
# main-be5add5996d6.
# --- lazy_counter (7 rules): counters that exist only after the bad event ----
landing_mirror_behind
column4: Counted only when a mirror push is refused (cog-github/src/landing.rs record_counter on the failure branch); no refusal in 24h means the counter was never created. The rule fires on the first one.

column1: mainline_delivery_preflight_refused
column4: Counted only when the preflight refuses a deploy (cog-reflection/src/mainline_deployer.rs); refused_total has no zero-value series until the first refusal.

column1: memory_backend_operation_never_succeeds
column4: Counted only on a failed memory backend operation (cog-memory/src/metrics_instrumented.rs); no error in the window means no series. The rule also requires memory_operations_total, which is present on the success path.

column1: redrive_budget_forgotten
column4: Read-side ledger loss is counted only when the ledger read fails (cog-github/src/landing.rs); today the read succeeds, so the {side="read"} series does not exist.

column1: redrive_charge_not_persisted
column4: Write-side ledger loss is counted only when the ledger write fails (cog-github/src/landing.rs); today the write succeeds, so the {side="write"} series does not exist.

column1: registry_tag_deletion_refused
column4: Counted only when a registry prune is refused (cog-reflection/src/mainline_deployer.rs); no refusal in the window.

column1: trace_tier_migration_failing
column4: Counted only when a trace-tier pass fails (cog-observability/src/snapshot.rs); no failure in the window.

column1: # --- error_only_state (3 rules): gauges exported only when unhealthy --------
declared_failure_class_unrecorded
column4: cog-collaboration/src/observable.rs emits this gauge only on the branch where a failure class could not be recorded; healthy operation exports nothing, which the rule reads as "no problem".

column1: held_series_check_unreadable
column4: cog-gateway/src/lib.rs exports this gauge only when the held-series check cannot be read; a readable check is absent, and the rule's max() sees no series.

column1: runtime_asset_content_drift
column4: cog-reflection/src/runtime_assets.rs exports state gauges only for problem states of destinations that have one; a healthy asset is absent. The check's own timestamp is a separate series (cogneva_runtime_asset_check_seconds, present).

column1: runtime_asset_not_refreshed
column4: Same gauge and same export rule; not_refreshed is absent because every checked asset matched its manifest.

column1: # --- code_not_deployed (1 rule, 4 series): newer than the running image -----
task_router_claim_stall
column4: The gauges were added in 221a6c22 (2026-10-19 10:56 +0800) and the running app image is main-be5add5996d6 (10:09 +0800), which predates them. They appear on the next rollout; delete this row then.
